class.name: ProjectSettings
class.brief_description: Subset of Godot's Project Settings added by this extension.

members.member:
Specifies the method FMOD Godot uses to access your source .bank files.
[b]Single Platform Build[/b] - You have a directory containing .bank files for a single platform. You specify the location of the directory in the Build Path setting.
[b]Multiple Platform Build[/b] - You have a directory containing .bank files for multiple platforms, with each platform in its own subdirectory. You specify the location of the top-level directory in the Build Path setting
Path to the FMOD Studio executable. Setting this is necessary for building banks from godot and the FMOD console.
Path to the FMOD Studio Project
Path to project folder to for bank files.

Only used by a Multiple Platform Build. Name of the subfolder of [member fmod/banks/import/bank_directory] that holds the banks your project uses in the editor, for example [code]pc[/code] (default) or [code]Desktop[/code]. Reference banks by their path in this folder. When exporting, each of its banks is replaced by the same bank from the most specific subfolder whose feature tags all match the export, for example [code]web[/code]. With Load banks set to All, the banks of this folder are loaded.
Controls automatic .bank file loading at startup time.
A list of .bank files to load at startup time. This list is only used if Load banks is set to Specified.
Pre-load audio sample data when loading .bank files via the Load banks setting. This will reduce latency whenever an event is played for the first time, at the cost of using more memory.
The key used in FMOD Studio to encrypt the .bank file sample data. Not compatible with loadBankMemory.
Controls the severity of log messages that FMOD produces. This only has an effect on development builds, as release builds don't use the logging version of FMOD.
Enables detailed statistics.
Enables display of additional information in logs.

Specifies when to accept connections to the game from FMOD Studio. This should be Disabled when releasing builds.
Disabled - Never accept connections from FMOD Studio.
Enabled - Always accept connections from FMOD Studio.
Development Build Only - Only accept connections from FMOD Studio when running a development build.
[b]Note:[/b] Live Update is not supported on the Web platform.
The network port that FMOD will use to accept connections from FMOD Studio.
The audio sample rate that FMOD's mixer should use. Lower sample rates reduce mixer CPU usage but also reduce audio quality.
The number of channels that will be audible. Lowering this count will reduce the FMOD mixer's CPU usage. See the virtual voice system document for more information.

The number of channels that can be played. Once the Real Channel Count is exceeded, the quietest channels will be virtualised, meaning they are not audible. See the virtual voice system document for more information.
The length of each DSP buffer. [b]Note:[/b] On the Web platform, the [code]fmod/general/dsp/buffer_length.web[/code] override (2048 by default, as recommended by FMOD for HTML5) is used instead.
The number of DSP buffers to use. [b]Note:[/b] On the Web platform, the [code]fmod/general/dsp/buffer_count.web[/code] override (2 by default, as recommended by FMOD for HTML5) is used instead.
A scaling factor for doppler shift.
A factor for converting game distance units to FMOD distance units.

A scaling factor for distance attenuation. When a sound uses a roll-off mode other than FMOD_3D_CUSTOMROLLOFF and the distance is greater than the sound's minimum distance, the distance is scaled by the roll-off scale.

FMOD plugin libraries to load when FMOD starts, mapped to their priority. Each key is the path to the library for the current platform: a [code]res://[/code] path, an absolute path, or a path relative to [member fmod/plugins/path]. Each platform needs its own build of a plugin (for example, "resonanceaudio.dll" on Windows and "libresonanceaudio.so" on Linux), so use feature overrides such as [code]fmod/plugins/plugins.windows[/code]. When exporting, the libraries are copied next to the executable (Windows, Linux), into [code]Contents/Frameworks[/code] (macOS) or into [code]lib/<abi>[/code] (Android) and loaded from there. On Android, each library must be in a folder named after its ABI, for example [code]arm64-v8a[/code]. [b]Note:[/b] Plugins are not supported on the Web platform, they are skipped with a warning.

Folder that relative paths in [member fmod/plugins/plugins] are resolved against. If empty, they are relative to the project folder ([code]res://[/code]). [b]Note:[/b] Plugins are not supported on the Web platform.

constants.constant: Enable informational, warning and error messages.
Verbose logging for memory operations, only use this if you are debugging a memory related issue.
Verbose logging for file access, only use this if you are debugging a file related issue.
Verbose logging for codec initialization, only use this if you are debugging a codec related issue.
Verbose logging for internal errors, use this for tracking the origin of error codes.
Verbose logging for whenever a Channel changes its virtual state.
Display the time stamp of the log message in milliseconds.
Display the source code file and line number for where the message originated.
Display the thread ID of the calling function that generated the message.
No .bank files will be loaded at initialization - you must handle all bank loading from script or by using the Bank Loader Node.
The .bank files in the Specified banks list will be loaded in order.
All .bank files will be loaded, in no particular order.
